new_objections.claim: R3 proposes to add a NEW translation key tools.names.applyPatch to all 10 translation files. The CodexPatch entry at knownTools.tsx:713 already uses t('tools.names.applyChanges').

The existing key is wired into the existing CodexPatch entry. Adding a parallel 'applyPatch' key creates two near-synonymous keys — a translation-files maintenance burden with no semantic benefit. AC3 says 'CodexPatch entry uses title: t(tools.names.applyPatch)' — but the current title is t('tools.names.applyChanges') and BA does not justify why renaming is required. This is a scope choice, not a blocking error: dev can either reuse the existing 'applyChanges' key (simpler — no translation files touched) or follow BA's spec literally and add the new key. Recommend BA pick the simpler path.
new_objections.required_evidence: BA should clarify: either (a) reuse t('tools.names.applyChanges') and remove R3 from the spec (no translation file edits needed; cycle becomes single-file change to knownTools.tsx), or (b) explicitly justify the rename and update all 10 translation files atomically with both keys aliased to the same string for one cycle of forward/backward compatibility.

new_objections.claim: BA does not mention that mcp__happy__change_title is already intercepted at the message-to-event layer in happy-app/sources/sync/reducer/messageToEvent.ts:28-31 (verbatim: 'if (block.type === tool-call && block.name === mcp__happy__change_title) ...').
new_objections.problem: QA grep found that messageToEvent.ts converts mcp__happy__change_title tool calls to service-message envelopes BEFORE they reach the knownTools renderer. This means the 'raw fallback card' that BA wants to suppress may not actually appear in Claude sessions today — the existing interceptor may already produce a 'Title changed to X' service message instead. If true, R2's added knownTools entry is defensive (belt-and-suspenders) but NOT a user-visible bug fix. AC2's GIVEN/WHEN/THEN may already pass without any change. This does NOT block dev — adding a hidden:true entry is harmless and provides defense-in-depth — but BA should acknowledge the existing interceptor and reframe AC2 as 'no regression' rather than 'fixes raw fallback card'.
new_objections.required_evidence: BA should add an Edge Case note: 'messageToEvent.ts:28-31 already intercepts mcp__happy__change_title and converts to service message. The new knownTools entry is defensive: if interception order changes or a tool-call envelope reaches the renderer, hidden:true prevents fallback. AC2 verifies no regression at either layer.'
